item.title: Latino Dems urge investment in Hinojosa campaign as Texas governor's race tightens
item.description: Latino Democratic leaders are renewing calls for the Democratic Governors Association to invest more heavily in Texas after a new poll showed Gina Hinojosa narrowly leading Republican Gov. Greg Abbott.

item.title: New information on FlyDubai cockpit flight; Russia continues attacks on Kyiv
item.description: CBS News national security analyst Aaron MacLean joins "The Takeout" to discuss what we know now about the co-pilot who allegedly tried to bring down a FlyDubai plane headed for Israel, the Iran war and Russia's latest attacks on Ukraine.

item.title: Defense attorney says Letitia James should recuse herself from Cornell investigation
item.description: An attorney for one of the seven men accused in the alleged sexual assault of a former Cornell University student​ at a fraternity house in 2024 is calling for Attorney General Letitia James to step down as special prosecutor.

item.title: 2 killed, including a student, in Central Florida school bus crash
item.description: A school bus was involved in a Central Florida crash Monday, killing two people, including a student, and several others were injured. Videos from the scene show the bus flipped onto its roof. CBS News correspondent Cristian Benavides reports.

item.title: Trump changes tune on mail-in voting, urges supporters to vote by mail as midterms near
item.description: President Trump is now urging his supporters to vote by mail if they can despite his previous claims about mail-in voting fraud. CBS News' Major Garrett, Ed O'Keefe and Anthony Salvanto have more on that, Mr. Trump's latest campaign rally in a red state and how poll numbers are shaping up with midterms rapidly approaching.

item.title: Ex-"American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn gets life sentence
item.description: Caleb Flynn was found guilty of killing his wife, Ashley, and attempting to blame the murder on a break-in at their home.

item.title: Battle with Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen tempers news on oil flow
item.description: Brent crude hovers around $100 a barrel despite news of increased Mideast oil flows, as Iran's Houthi allies battle over control of Red Sea shipping lanes.

item.title: Coca-Cola reveals new flavors for Coke, Powerade and other brands
item.description: Coca-Cola said it will roll out the new flavors, all fruit-inspired, in 2027. Here's what the beverage giant is planning.

item.title: Former Anthropic researcher doubles down on AI warning in testimony
item.description: Whistleblowers sounded the alarm over the potential threat artificial intelligence poses at a landmark hearing before the New York City Council on Monday. Representatives from OpenAI, Google and other big tech companies also testified as city lawmakers considered AI safeguards. CBS News' Lauren Fichten reports. Anthony Ha, a TechCrunch editor, also joins CBS News to discuss President Trump's formation of an AI "Super Intelligence Force."

item.title: Former "American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn sentenced to life in prison for wife's murder
item.description: A judge in Ohio sentenced former "American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn to life in prison on Monday. Last Tuesday, a jury found Flynn guilty of murdering his wife while she was sleeping in February of this year. CBS News correspondent Ian Lee reports.

item.title: Supreme Court wrestles with energy companies' bid to block major climate suit
item.description: Eight of the nine justices heard nearly two hours of oral arguments in a case involving an effort by the city and county of Boulder, Colorado, to hold energy companies accountable for the effects of global climate change.

item.title: Trump sending ACA and Medicare checks, but will they offset costs?
item.description: President Trump sent $500 checks to some Affordable Care Act enrollees, while 20 million Medicare recipients will soon get $90 checks. Will they make a difference?

item.title: Israel was prepared to shoot down FlyDubai plane, sources say
item.description: Israel was ready to implement a long-practiced protocol after the captain of a FlyDubai plane was attacked in the cockpit, Israeli sources told CBS News.

item.title: Brian Jeansonne on living beyond his ALS prognosis
item.description: Author Brian Jeansonne was given five years to live when doctors diagnosed him with ALS. Six and a half years later, Jeansonne is continuing his battle. Jeansonne and his son and caregiver, Nate, join CBS News to discuss how they've approached life since that diagnosis.

item.title: Russia plays down reported plague lab death and says, trust us
item.description: A Russian plague lab worker died of "pneumonia of unknown origin," officials say, in response to initial reports that she was exposed to the deadly bacteria during a lab accident.

item.title: Amber Guyger granted parole after serving 7 years for murder of Botham Jean
item.description: Guyger, who faced anywhere from five years to up to life in prison, was sentenced to 10 years.

item.title: British Airways flight drops 27,000 feet, returns to London
item.description: A spokesperson for British Airways said there was a technical issue and that the aircraft later landed safely.

item.title: Supreme Court to focus on climate case, immigration in new term
item.description: The Supreme Court's new term began Monday, where it's expected to tackle a high-stakes climate case and the Trump administration's immigration crackdown. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson has more.

item.title: Why is a Republican super PAC diverting millions to Kansas?
item.description: One of the largest Republican super PACs is diverting millions of dollars to Kansas as the Senate race between Democrat Adam Hamilton and incumbent Roger Marshall heats up. CBS News' Fin Gomez has the latest.

item.title: Musk's data centers push out family that's owned land for generations
item.description: A plant in Southaven, Mississippi, that powers Elon Musk's SpaceXAI data centers in the area has sparked backlash from residents concerned about noise and air pollution.

item.title: Mayor to homeowner losing sleep over data center plant: "Consider selling"
item.description: Noise from a Mississippi plant powering Elon Musk's xAI data centers in the area is causing migraines, ringing ears and sleepless nights, residents say.

item.title: 2 dead, including student, in Central Florida school bus crash, sheriff says
item.description: Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd said an oncoming car crossed the center line and caused the crash in Winter Haven, Florida.

item.title: When to book Thanksgiving and Christmas flights for the best deals
item.description: Knowing when to buy plane tickets for holiday season travel can save you money. Here's the optimal time to book this year as airfares rise.

item.title: Gatorade sold in dozens of states recalled due to undeclared dyes
item.description: Recalled Gatorade sold in 37 states could cause temporary "adverse health consequences," a federal regulatory agency says.

item.title: Dennis Hastert, disgraced former House speaker, dies at 84
item.description: Former Speaker of the House Dennis Hastert represented Illinois for two decades in Congress and was later jailed on charges related to his concealment of hush money payments made to cover up sexual abuse.

item.title: Japanese leader calls woman's murder, allegedly by U.S. Marine, "heinous crime"
item.description: A woman's murder allegedly committed by a U.S. Marine​ in Okinawa is a "heinous crime," Japan's premier said on Monday, as the new accusation of violence involving American forces sparked public outrage.

item.title: Experts are training AI on how to do their jobs
item.description: It's become a booming industry: teaching artificial intelligence how to get better at doing all kinds of jobs. As AI advances, many fear what this tech means for the future of work.

item.title: The Alito Court: A rare interview with the influential Supreme Court justice
item.description: Justice Samuel Alito discussed his opinion in the Dobbs decision overturning Roe v. Wade, the leaked draft and its aftermath, same-sex marriage rights and why he's not retiring yet.

item.title: Key Biden aide recalls "draconian measures" being considered against Israel
item.description: In a CBS News interview, Biden-era Middle East adviser Brett McGurk recounted the administration's response to the Oct. 7 attack, its handling of the Israel-Hamas war, the role of Iran and the long-sought push to normalize relations between Israel and Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Will AI harm humans? Poll finds Americans want to slow development but not stop
item.description: Americans are optimistic about scientific advances in AI, but concerned that AI may take jobs.
